newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks end grim day down, but off lows.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks end grim day down, but off lows.

text.p: South African shares ended a grim Thursday down for the fourth consecutive session, hit by a wave of negative sentiment that has sent prices tumbling, dealers said.
The market is worried over confusing signals from government and the Reserve Bank on scrapping exchange controls and rising fears of an interest rate hike.
A recent spate of poor results from groups like retailer Edgars and Coke bottler ABI has added to the gloom.

The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) has suffered badly in the wake of the most recent rand collapse. In quieter periods the JSE tends to track Wall Street, but the market is now steadfastly focused on its domestic hard times and has ignored record breaking surges in New York.

As trades flowed through after the close of trade the all-share index climbed a little from its day lows, but still ended at 6,802.9, down 71.0 points, as industrials slid to 8,014.4, down 77.1 points.
Gold shares, which were resilient earlier in the week, suffered a second bad day running. The golds index fell nine points to 1,693.0 over ears on a jittery bullion price.
